Metacells with SEACells and mcRigor gamma optimization

metacells_seacells.Rmd

When the starting point is single-cell data, cellprograms can aggregate cells into metacells — transcriptomically homogeneous small groups — before pseudobulk factorization. Metacells are built with SEACells (run in an isolated, pinned basilisk Python environment built on first use) and QC’d with mcRigor, stratified so that metacells never cross the grouping variables (donor x cell type by default).

This vignette runs the full workflow on a simulated dataset with planted cell-type identity, then feeds the metacell counts into fit_celltype_programs().

Simulate a small single-cell dataset

Two donors x two cell types, 80 cells each, 200 genes. Each cell type gets a private marker block; everything else is background Poisson noise.

library(cellprograms)
set.seed(11)

n_per <- 80
types <- c("Tcells", "Bcells")
donors <- c("donor1", "donor2")
groups <- rep(paste0(rep(donors, each = length(types)), "_", rep(types, length(donors))),
              each = n_per)

lam <- matrix(0.5, nrow = 200, ncol = length(groups))
markers <- list(Tcells = 1:12, Bcells = 13:24)
for (g in unique(groups)) {
  type <- sub(".*_", "", g)
  cols <- which(groups == g)
  lam[markers[[type]], cols] <- 8
}
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(rpois(200 * length(groups), as.vector(lam)),
                         nrow = 200, ncol = length(groups), sparse = TRUE)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(200))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(length(groups)))

meta <- data.frame(
  donor = sub("_.*", "", groups),
  celltype = sub(".*_", "", groups),
  row.names = colnames(counts)
)

obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, meta.data = meta)
obj <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(obj, nfeatures = 60, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::ScaleData(obj, verbose = FALSE)
obj <- Seurat::RunPCA(obj, npcs = 10, verbose = FALSE)

Build metacells per group

MetacellsByGroupsSEACells() fits SEACells separately within each group.by stratum and stores everything under the Seurat object’s misc:

obj <- MetacellsByGroupsSEACells(obj,
                                 group.by = c("donor", "celltype"),
                                 cells_per_metacell = 20,
                                 min_cells = 50,
                                 n_top_genes = 60,
                                 n_pc = 10,
                                 seed = 11, verbose = FALSE)
res <- GetMetacellSEACells(obj)
names(res)

The result carries the metacell Seurat object, the soft (cells x archetypes) assignment matrix, per-metacell mcRigor QC, fit statistics, the parameters used, and any skipped groups:

head(res$qc)                 # mcDiv, dubious flag, ZeroRate per metacell
res$skipped_groups           # groups dropped (e.g. too few cells) - usually empty

Groups with too few cells (below min_cells) are skipped with a warning rather than failing the call, and degenerate SEACells fits (all hard assignments collapsing to one archetype) drop that group’s soft assignments gracefully — check skipped_groups when working with small strata.

Optimize the number of metacells (gamma)

SEACells’ gamma is the number of archetypes — the granularity. OptimizeGammaSEACells() refits SEACells across candidate gammas per group and picks the winner by the mcRigor optimization score:

opt <- OptimizeGammaSEACells(obj,
                             group.by = "donor",
                             gammas = c(10, 20),
                             n_top_genes = 60,
                             n_pc = 10,
                             min_cells = 50,
                             mcrigor_args = list(Nrep = 5),
                             seed = 11, verbose = FALSE)
opt$optimal_gamma            # winning gamma per donor group
opt$scores                   # mcRigor score per gamma x group

Gammas whose membership labels degenerate (fewer than two distinct labels after Seurat v5 aggregation) are dropped with a warning and excluded from the pick rather than crashing the run.

Metacell counts feed the program fit directly 

mc <- res$metacell_object
counts_mc <- SeuratObject::LayerData(mc[["RNA"]], layer = "counts")  # genes x metacells
by_type <- split(colnames(mc), mc$celltype)
pb <- lapply(by_type, function(cells) t(as.matrix(counts_mc[, cells, drop = FALSE])))

x <- as_cell_program_data(pb)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(x, loading_prior = "point_laplace",
                             max_factors = 4, features = "variable",
                             n_variable_genes = 100)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
program_summary(fit)[, c("cell_type", "n_programs", "R2", "elbo")]

The planted structure survives the aggregation: each cell type’s programs are dominated by its private marker block.

marker_expr <- as.matrix(counts_mc[unlist(markers), , drop = FALSE])
marker_expr <- t(scale(t(marker_expr)))
df <- data.frame(
  metacell = factor(colnames(marker_expr), levels = colnames(marker_expr)),
  gene = rep(rownames(marker_expr), times = ncol(marker_expr)),
  z = as.vector(marker_expr)
)
ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(metacell, gene, fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "metacell", y = "marker gene") +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6))
